# R138 — Modular Farey gaps, sharp all-gap saturation and coefficient-semigroup persistence

2026-11-14 (Asia/Shanghai). Status: AUTHOR-SIDE MATHEMATICS / NOT_REVIEWED. Frozen scientific source pin: 43ec6098b1330ae86d0a7863be336c5d97f6ef34. Predecessor: R137B and R137C, immutable GitHub commit ab486d53fad5fdeb15b6c8647b6778b8b1e1b093. This is an external tied-phase S23 auxiliary observer; no native X6/three-dimensional-slice transfer is claimed.

## Problem and definitions

For integers K ≥ 2 and m ≥ 1, L=K−1, the observed m-bit word is

\[
S_i^{(K)}(\theta)=\lfloor(L+i+1)\theta\rfloor-\lfloor(L+i)\theta\rfloor,\qquad 0\le i<m,\quad 0<\theta<1.
\]

Take two neighboring Farey fractions a/b<c/d of order m (bc−ad=1), and one consecutive pair of intercept cuts inside their open slope interval:

\[
G_\ell(\alpha)=p-j\alpha,\qquad G_u(\alpha)=q-k\alpha,\quad 0\le j,k\le m.
\]

Synthetic bottom/top cuts are (0,0), (1,0). The cuts are distinct and strictly ordered in the open interval. R137B proves that this specified gap is realized at phase \(\rho=\{L\alpha\}\) iff some integer N lies strictly inside

\[
(A_K,B_K)=((L+k)a/b-q,\ (L+j)c/d-p). \tag{1}
\]

Its existing midpoint construction gives a rational witness for every feasible gap. Rational endpoint words have open-gap representatives by R137B's right-continuity argument.

Set
\[
D=jbc-kad+(q-p)bd,\qquad h_K=((L+k)a)\bmod b\in\{0,\ldots,b-1\}.
\]

## R138.1 — Fraction-free exact modular criterion

**The gap is feasible if and only if**
\[
\boxed{L+D>d(b-h_K).} \tag{2}
\]

Proof. The Farey determinant implies \(bd(B_K-A_K)=L+D\). The least integer strictly larger than A is \(\lfloor A_K\rfloor+1\), whose distance above A is \((b-h_K)/b\), including the case h=0. This integer lies below B precisely when \(B_K-A_K>(b-h_K)/b\). Multiply by bd to obtain (2). Strict equality is correctly infeasible. The predicate uses only a remainder and integer arithmetic for any bit length of K. Source inventory and witness recovery costs remain accounted for separately.

## R138.2 — A lower bound for every intercept-gap offset

**For every consecutive gap,**
\[
\boxed{D\ge \min(b,d).} \tag{3}
\]

Proof. At the Farey endpoints, the nonnegative integer gaps are
\[
T_r=b[G_u(a/b)-G_\ell(a/b)]\ge0,\qquad
T_s=d[G_u(c/d)-G_\ell(c/d)]\ge0.
\]
The affine cuts cannot reverse order at the endpoints by continuity. Expanding with bc−ad=1 yields the two exact identities
\[
\boxed{D=dT_r+j=bT_s+k.} \tag{4}
\]
If D<min(b,d), the first identity forces T_r=0,j=D; the second forces T_s=0,k=D. Hence j=k and, since the endpoint gap vanishes, p=q. The two affine cuts would be identical, contradicting their distinct consecutive status. The argument covers synthetic boundary cuts.

## R138.3 — Sharp universal all-gap saturation

For m≥2 define
\[
\boxed{U_{\rm gap}(m)=(m-1)^2+2.} \tag{5}
\]

**For every integer K≥U_gap(m), every individual consecutive intercept gap of every Farey cell of order m is feasible. Moreover, U_gap is the least coefficient from which this all-gap property holds forever.**

Proof. Neighboring Farey denominators satisfy 1≤b,d≤m. Except for b=d=1, they are unequal, so \(bd-\min(b,d)\le(m-1)^2\). Combining this with (3), \(bd-D\le(m-1)^2\). For K≥U_gap, L>(m−1)², and therefore \(L+D>bd\ge d(b-h_K)\). Formula (2) realizes every gap.

For sharpness, the Farey cell \(1/m<1/(m-1)\) has a consecutive intercept gap with lower cut 0 and upper cut \(1-(m-1)\alpha\). Its exact data are
\[
(a,b,c,d,p,j,q,k)=(1,m,1,m-1,0,0,1,m-1),\quad D=m-1.
\]
At \(K=(m-1)^2+1\), L=(m−1)² and \((L+k)a\bmod b=0\). Thus \(L+D=m(m-1)=d(b-h_K)\). The strict inequality (2) fails: this specific gap is missing at U_gap−1. For m=1, K=2 already realizes both gaps, the minimum K in the declared domain.

**Corollary.** Because all finite Sturmian words of length m arise from these gaps (R137B), the complete language occurs for all \(K\ge(m-1)^2+2\). This improves R135's sufficient threshold \(m(m-1)+1\) by m−2 (m≥3). Sharpness in (5) concerns **every gap**, not the word-language eventual threshold: distinct gaps may represent the same word.

## R138.4 — Two-generator coefficient persistence

For a fixed Farey cell and one of its gaps, write G(K) when the gap is feasible. Then for every u,v≥0 integers,
\[
\boxed{G(K)\Longrightarrow G(K+ub+vd).} \tag{6}
\]

Proof. A shift of K by b changes interval (1) from (A,B) to \((A+a,B+a+1/d)\); its integer witness N becomes N+a. A shift by d changes it to \((A+c-1/b,B+c)\); N becomes N+c. Iteration proves (6), including constructive transport of integer witness candidates. The Farey denominators are coprime, so every integer \(t\ge (b-1)(d-1)\) belongs to the semigroup generated by b and d (Frobenius conductor, with the b=1 or d=1 case immediate).

For all m≥2, K≥2 and any integer \(t\ge(m-1)(m-2)\), applying this semigroup representation gapwise gives
\[
\boxed{V(K,m)\subseteq V(K+t,m).} \tag{7}
\]
Also, at least one of b,d is at most m−1. Therefore, writing \(P_n=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n)\), the shift \(P_{m-1}\) is a multiple of one of the two period generators for every gap:
\[
\boxed{V(K,m)\subseteq V(K+P_{m-1},m).} \tag{8}
\]
This strengthens R137C's guaranteed P_m step; for m=p^e (prime power), \(P_m/P_{m-1}=p\). Equation (8) does not assert minimality of this common shift.

## R138.5 — Exact eventual K threshold for one specified gap

Fix a gap and for each residue r=0,...,b−1 define
\[
h_r=((r+k)a)\bmod b,\qquad H_r=d(b-h_r)-D.
\]
On this residue, all L≥1 are L=r+bt for integers t≥t_min, with t_min=1 if r=0 and 0 otherwise. By (2), exactly the infeasible members satisfy
\[
t\le\left\lfloor\frac{H_r-r}{b}\right\rfloor.
\]
If this upper bound is below t_min there is no bad member on that residue. Otherwise the largest bad L is \(L_r=r+b\lfloor(H_r-r)/b\rfloor\). Let B be the largest of these L_r, if any. Then the exact smallest integer K_e for which this **specified gap** is realized at every K≥K_e is
\[
\boxed{K_e=2\ \text{if no bad L exists; otherwise}\quad K_e=B+2.} \tag{9}
\]
Evaluating this formula costs O(b) integer operations, with only coefficients of O(log(m+K))-bit size at the query boundary. To determine a **word**'s threshold, combine its multiple gap representations rather than transferring a single-gap threshold unconditionally.

## Exact verification

Companion check_r138.py independently compares (2) to the original rational interval test, checks returned witnesses by the original strict fractional-part formula, and checks denominator-shift inclusions. It also reconstructs finite first/eventual full-word thresholds for m=1..20, agreeing with the R136 recorded cases. Exact testing used Python integers and Fraction; the separate proof above establishes the universal statements. Run marker: R138_MODULAR_SEMIGROUP_PASS.

Validation counts: 6,560 modular/rational comparisons; 1,282 two-form witness checks; 39,944 individual +b/+d checks; 290 global P_(m−1) inclusion comparisons; 15,312 D≥min(b,d) instances; 19 sharp all-gap boundary checks for m=2..20; 1,172 exact gap eventual-cutoff checks. The finite threshold sweep reproduces m=5 (7,7), 7 (11,16), 10 (25,33), 12 (41,51), 15 (67,92), 18 (99,129), 20 (113,163) for first/eventual full-language saturation.

## Next unresolved question

Find the *word-level* exact eventual coefficient through union of its multiple Farey-gap residue progressions, without enumerating every K through a quadratic window. Classify the least universal positive coefficient shift for word inclusion, and investigate general signed, offset-tied S23 phase classes. Maintain the external-observer versus native X6 typing boundary. Independent mathematical review remains NOT_REVIEWED.
